face_semantics: roster('support_a') trains on Support-B and evaluates on Support-A; _evaluate applies the Program to training rows only, so a gain of exactly zero on a face means the Program left that face's *training* series untouched

training_corpus_by_origin.reading: every anchor clears anchor + 48 <= origin at each swept origin and no P4 path overrides the anchor list, so the Program's intervention is the same corpus at all six; only the evaluation window moves

outlier_iqr_zero_reading_explained.earlier_claim: reported as 'Support-A aggregate gain exactly +0.000 at all six origins', flagged as a possible third instrument fault
outlier_iqr_zero_reading_explained.cause_of_the_misreport: the reporting expression coerced a missing aggregate_gain to zero with `(value or 0)`, so a refusal printed as +0.000
outlier_iqr_zero_reading_explained.operator_is_not_a_no_op: outlier_iqr moves 1042 points across 108 of 200 training windows on the Support-B corpus, so the refusal is about one window's modification fraction, not about the operator doing nothing

window_verifier_is_all_or_nothing.rule: ScopeExecutor._verify runs verify_candidate independently on every training window that will actually execute; a single rejected window refuses the whole program on that face
window_verifier_is_all_or_nothing.consequence: one window out of 200 over the cap refuses the program at every origin, because the training corpus is identical across origins; this gates the effective Program Space on worst-case single-window behaviour rather than on utility or risk
window_verifier_is_all_or_nothing.observed_instance: outlier_iqr on the support_a face, 1 of 200 windows

consumer_is_fitted_once_per_program_and_.why: _evaluate builds x_train/y_train only from training windows, and those are identical at every swept origin; the Ridge fit therefore does not depend on the origin at all -- only x_eval and the truth slice move
consumer_is_fitted_once_per_program_and_.implication: the six origins are six evaluation windows of ONE fitted model, not six independent replications of the intervention; a cross-origin claim is a statement about one model's benefit across six future windows
consumer_is_fitted_once_per_program_and_.does_not_invalidate: the origin-2856 result stands as stated -- a model trained on period_median_complete>outlier_* prepared data beats the identity-trained model on both disjoint series groups there
consumer_is_fitted_once_per_program_and_.affects_experiment_design: adding new origins past 900 gives a new evaluation window but the same training corpus and the same intervention; genuine external validation must also move the anchor set or the training series
